_comment: What each trail-maintaining organisation actually publishes, beyond the geometry already in trail_orgs.json (#1543 follow-on). The A.T. reaches a hiker with shelters, water, closures and a club section map; every other trail in the catalogue reaches them as a line and a name. This file is the survey of what would close that gap, harvested 2026-09-29 from each organisation's own site.
_method: Each organisation's homepage was read and every same-host link classified by what it leads to. The pages behind the map, conditions and places links were then read one level deeper for anything a pipeline could ingest without a human in the middle - a feed, a GPX or KML file, an ArcGIS item id, a CalTopo or Avenza map. Nothing here was fetched from a third-party aggregator, and nothing was inferred: a row lists a link only where that link is on the organisation's own page.
_what_this_is_not: NOT a licence finding and NOT a decision to load anything. trail_orgs.json's `licence_basis` and `load` still govern what may be fetched, and a published page is not a grant. This says what exists; that file says what may be taken.
_the_gap_this_measures: MEASURED across the 46 stewards: 38 publish maps or a guidebook, 36 a membership or join page, 30 a conditions or closures page, 25 a page about shelters, campsites, water or parking, and 26 a store. 31 yielded something machine-readable one level down. The A.T. is not unusual in what its steward publishes - it is unusual in that OurHike already reads it.
_closure_feeds_are_the_short_path: Four organisations publish trail closures as an RSS feed on their own site: ATC (already read), the Arizona Trail Association, Connecticut Forest & Park Association for the New England Trail, and the Florida Trail Association. A feed is a closure the app could carry without anybody transcribing it, which is the same shape as the A.T. update path this app already has.
_third_party_guide_is_somebody_elses: Ten organisations link to a FarOut guide, several of them water reports. Those are a commercial publisher's data under its own terms, not the steward's, and they are recorded here only so nobody mistakes the link on an org's page for the org publishing the data. @unvalidated - nobody has read FarOut's terms.
